transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-approval huddle. As you know, the district's middle-school mathematics assessment is scheduled for May 14, 2027, and I've asked each of you to review the draft administration plan before I give it final approval. The plan currently calls for digital testing on school tablets, all 26 students testing together in Room 201, one proctor, graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, and completed materials stored in the general records cabinet. I'd like to go through each component systematically. Could each of you share your review findings, starting with any concerns you've identified?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I need to flag a concern with the room arrangement in the draft plan. My finalized roster does have 26 students, but the state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students. I've already prepared Room 201 for 14 students and Room 202 for the remaining 12 students to comply with that requirement. However, I should note that this updated room plan has not yet been entered into the district tracker, so the draft plan still reflects all 26 students together in Room 201.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I need to flag a concern with the calculator provision in the draft plan. During my review of the current state mathematics assessment manual this week, I found that calculators may be used only on section 2 of the assessment, and they must be four-function calculators — not graphing calculators. The draft plan currently calls for graphing calculators available throughout the entire assessment, which would be non-compliant on both counts. I have not yet amended the draft plan to reflect these requirements.

However, this result has not yet been added to the plan, so the draft still calls for digital testing on school tablets.

I have not yet updated the storage field in the draft plan to reflect the necessary changes.

transcript.text: Thank you all for your thorough reviews. Each of you has identified a critical compliance issue with the draft plan, and I appreciate you flagging these before I give final approval. Let me summarize what I'm hearing: Mr. Bell, the room capacity must be split into Room 201 for 14 students and Room 202 for 12 students per state manual limits. Ms. Shah, calculators must be four-function only and limited to section 2 of the assessment. Mr. Nguyen, the tablets can't run the secure testing application, so we need to switch to paper booklets as authorized by the vendor. Ms. Delgado, completed materials must be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days. Before I settle on the revised plan, I want to address one more component — the draft currently calls for one proctor. Given that we're now splitting students across two rooms, does anyone have concerns about whether one proctor is sufficient, or are there state requirements regarding proctor-to-student ratios or proctors per testing room that I should be aware of?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, that's an important question. I don't have specific information about state requirements regarding proctor-to-student ratios or proctors per testing room beyond the room capacity limit of 14 students that I've already flagged. However, from a practical testing administration standpoint, splitting 26 students across two rooms — Room 201 with 14 and Room 202 with 12 — with only one proctor would seem to present a significant supervision challenge. A single proctor cannot be in two rooms simultaneously, so we may need to consider assigning a second proctor or finding another compliant solution. I'd recommend we confirm whether the state manual addresses this before finalizing the plan.
